input: What do these audits actually involve, and how do they ensure accuracy?
output:
Here’s what the Maryland post-election audits involve and how they aim to ensure accuracy:

- What it involves
  - After each general election, Maryland conducts an independent automated post-election tabulation audit of every ballot cast (early voting, election day, absentee, provisional) using ballot images captured by the primary voting system. An independent software (ClearAudit) re-tabulates these images, and the results are compared to the official reported results; any discrepancies are resolved by elections officials [PostElectionTabulationAuditLegislativeReport](https://elections.maryland.gov/press_room/documents/PostElectionTabulationAuditLegislativeReport.pdf).
  - The audit is ballot-level, aims to use securely stored ballot images rather than handling physical ballots, and is conducted to complete before certification and swearing-in. It is designed to be independent of the primary voting system [PostElectionTabulationAuditLegislativeReport](https://elections.maryland.gov/press_room/documents/PostElectionTabulationAuditLegislativeReport.pdf).
  - The program has included pilot testing of three methodologies (independent automated audit, ballot-level risk-limiting audit, and a fixed-percentage audit) to evaluate which best supports accuracy, reliability, and efficiency, with criteria such as minimizing staff time and ensuring the audit is completed on time [PostElectionTabulationAuditLegislativeReport](https://elections.maryland.gov/press_room/documents/PostElectionTabulationAuditLegislativeReport.pdf).
  - It is not a recount; post-election audits verify the voting system’s performance, not to automatically change winners [PostElectionTabulationAuditLegislativeReport](https://elections.maryland.gov/press_room/documents/PostElectionTabulationAuditLegislativeReport.pdf).

- How it ensures accuracy
  - Using an independent audit tool to re-tabulate ballot images provides a separate check on the primary system’s results, increasing confidence in outcomes [PostElectionTabulationAuditLegislativeReport](https://elections.maryland.gov/press_room/documents/PostElectionTabulationAuditLegislativeReport.pdf).
  - Comparing two separate tallies (the primary system vs. the independent tally) generates data points to identify and resolve discrepancies before certification [PostElectionTabulationAuditLegislativeReport](https://elections.maryland.gov/press_room/documents/PostElectionTabulationAuditLegislativeReport.pdf).
  - The process emphasizes securely stored ballot images and, where possible, ballot-level validation to minimize custody issues and human error; however, some sources note that image-based audits may need additional manual validation against physical ballots to ensure image fidelity and trustworthiness. Maryland discusses adding manual validation or sample hand checks to bolster confidence when using digital images alone [PostElectionTabulationAuditLegislativeReport](https://elections.maryland.gov/press_room/documents/PostElectionTabulationAuditLegislativeReport.pdf).
